title: Waqf in An-Naba': stopping on fathatan and the ayah ends: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: An-Naba' and Al-Qadr as a model
source: Written for quran/y7 lesson 43 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Waqf in An-Naba' rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 43. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Madd 'iwad
points: Fathatan at a stop becomes aa
Dammatan and kasratan: drop the vowel at a stop

arabic.text: لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًۭا وَلَا شَرَابًا (٢٤)

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
the long aa that replaces fathatan at a stop

questions.q: Recite 78:6 to 11 stopping at every ayah end with madd 'iwad.
questions.a: mihaadaa, awtaadaa, azwaajaa, subaataa, libaasaa, ma'aashaa.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: write the stopped form of ten ayah endings from 78:1 to 32. Today's rota group recites 78:1 to 32.
Extend: recite 78:24 with an emergency stop after «بَرْدًۭا» and a correct restart.
Stretch: why is madd 'iwad two counts and not six?
questions.a: It replaces the tanween with a natural alif: a natural madd of two counts.
A) awtaadaa. Fathatan at a stop: madd 'iwad, two counts.

questions.q: Think again: Almost every ayah of An-Naba' ends in -aa. What would go wrong if you said '-an' at each stop?
questions.a: That is the joined form; at a stop the tanween on fathah becomes a two-count aa (madd 'iwad).
